parts.text: A student is investigating refraction using a transparent block. Fig. 3.1 shows the first stage of the student’s ray trace. ABCD is the outline of the transparent block. E is at the centre of AB and G is at the centre of CD . Fig. 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) On Fig. 3.1, draw a line FE to the left of the normal, above the outline of the block, and at an angle i = 20° to the normal. [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) • The student places a pin P on the line FE , at a suitable distance from the block. • There is a vertical line L 1 drawn on side AB of the block at point E . There is a second vertical line L 2 drawn on side CD at point G . • The student observes the images of L 1 and P through side CD of the block. He carefully turns the block to the dashed position in Fig. 3.1. In this position the vertical line L 2 and the images of L 1 and P appear one behind the other.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) On Fig. 3.1, mark with a cross (×) a suitable position for pin P. [1]

ms.label: 3(b)(i)
ms.text: P at least 5 cm from the block

ms.label: 3(b)(ii)
ms.text:
Greater accuracy with greater distance owtte
OR easier to line up accurately

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) On Fig. 3.1, measure the angle θ and enter it in the first row of Table 3.1, on page 10. [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) • The student measures the angle θ between the original position of AB and the new position of AB , as indicated in Fig. 3.1. • He repeats the procedure, using values of i = 30°, 40°, 50° and 60°. • The readings are shown in Table 3.1. parts.text: (d) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ...........................................................[2]
